examples.ko: 어머니가 입원하셔서 제가 간병을 하고 있어요.
examples.en: My mother is in the hospital, so I am looking after her.
It is not easy to find a caregiver.

examples.ko: 간병 때문에 한 달 동안 휴가를 냈어요.
examples.en: I took a month off to take care of a patient.
I checked at the hospital how much caregiving costs.
I got really worn out taking care of my father.
The family decided to take turns caring for the patient.

explain: '간호'는 환자를 치료하며 돌보는 일까지 넓게 쓰고, '간병'은 환자 곁에서 먹고 씻는 것을 도우며 돌보는 일에 써요. '간병인', '간병비'처럼 함께 쓰는 말이 많아요.

phrases.example: 간병인이 하루 종일 할머니를 돌봐 드려요.
phrases.en: A caregiver looks after my grandmother all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자를 돌보는 일을 하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person whose job is caring for a patient.

phrases.en: I'm worried because caregiving costs a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자를 돌보는 데 드는 돈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the money spent on caring for a patient.

phrases.en: I've been caring for my father for several months now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 바꾸면 '간병을 하다'보다 짧고 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a verb, it is shorter and more natural than 간병을 하다.
phrases.en_equiv: to nurse; to care for a patient

explain_en: '간호' (nursing) can include medical care, while '간병' means staying by a patient and helping with things like eating and washing. It appears in set words such as '간병인' (caregiver) and '간병비' (care costs).

examples.en: The mosquito bite keeps itching.
My throat tickled, so I drank some water.
My nose tickled, and then I sneezed.
My back is itchy. Can you scratch it for me?
My hair touched the back of my neck and it tickled.
As the wound healed, it began to itch.

explain: '간지럽다'가 일반적인 말이고, '간질거리다'는 간질간질한 느낌이 계속될 때 써요. 사람이 일부러 간지럽게 하는 건 '간질이다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My nose is tickling, so I'm sneezing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간지러운 느낌이 이어질 때 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word for a continuing tickling feeling.

phrases.en: My back itched, so I scratched it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 기본적인 말이고 어디서든 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic word, usable anywhere.

phrases.en: My eyes itch so much I can't stand it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연결형 '-아서'를 붙여 이유와 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아서 links a reason to a result.

explain_en: '간지럽다' is the general word, while '간질거리다' is used when the tickly feeling keeps going. When a person deliberately tickles someone, the word is '간질이다'.

en: to cup; to hold in one's hands

examples.ko: 추운 날 따뜻한 컵을 두 손으로 감싸쥐었어요.
examples.en: On the cold day, I cupped a warm mug in both hands.
The child grabbed the knee that got hurt in the fall and cried.

examples.ko: 그는 얼굴을 감싸쥔 채 한참 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He sat for a long time with his face in his hands.
It's a little less cold if you cup your hands.

examples.ko: 배가 아파서 배를 감싸쥐며 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My stomach hurt, so I went to the hospital holding my belly.

examples.ko: 작은 새를 다치지 않게 살며시 감싸쥐세요.
examples.en: Gently cup the little bird in your hands so it isn't hurt.

explain: 손으로 무언가를 둘러싸듯 잡을 때 써요. 아픈 곳을 손으로 잡는 장면에도 자주 나와요. 꽉 힘을 주는 '움켜쥐다'와 달리 부드럽게 감싸는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I held my head in my hands when I saw the test result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정이나 고민이 클 때 하는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a gesture made when very worried or troubled.
phrases.en_equiv: to hold one's head in one's hands

phrases.example: 차가운 내 손을 그가 감싸쥐어 주었어요.
phrases.en: He wrapped my cold hands in his.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람의 손을 따뜻하게 잡아 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when warmly holding another person's hand.

phrases.en: I was startled and clutched my chest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 아플 때 몸을 손으로 잡는 장면에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for gripping a part of the body when startled or in pain.

explain_en: It is used when you hold something by wrapping your hands around it, and it often appears in scenes of holding a sore spot. Unlike '움켜쥐다', which means gripping hard, it feels soft and enclosing.

examples.en: Training is tomorrow, so I have to pack my field gear.
My field pack is so heavy that my shoulders hurt.

examples.ko: 군장 검사가 있어서 모두 일찍 일어났어요.
examples.en: There was a gear inspection, so everyone got up early.

examples.ko: 동생이 군대에서 군장 싸는 법을 배웠대요.
examples.en: I heard my brother learned how to pack his field gear in the army.

examples.ko: 행군 때는 군장에 물과 간식을 넣어 가요.
examples.en: On a march, they put water and snacks in their field pack.

examples.ko: 군장은 가능하면 가볍게 꾸리는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to pack your field gear as light as possible.

explain: 군인이 훈련이나 행군 때 메고 가는 가방과 장비 전체를 말해요. 일반 가방은 '배낭'이라고 하고, '군장'은 군대 이야기에서 '군장을 싸다', '군장을 메다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I woke up early in the morning and packed my military gear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훈련이나 행군 전에 장비를 가방에 넣어 준비한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to pack gear into the bag before training or a march.

phrases.example: 군장을 메고 한 시간 넘게 걸었어요.
phrases.en: I walked for over an hour carrying my military pack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군장을 어깨에 지고 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes carrying the military pack on one's shoulders.

phrases.en: Marching with full gear was really hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 장비를 모두 갖춘 군장을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a pack with all the required equipment.

explain_en: It means the whole bag and equipment a soldier carries for training or marches. An ordinary backpack is a '배낭'; '군장' appears in army talk as '군장을 싸다' or '군장을 메다'.

examples.en: The child has a fever and groans in its sleep.
I grunted while moving the heavy box.
The puppy is whining in front of the door.
Don't just moan; take medicine if it hurts.

examples.ko: 어려운 수학 문제 앞에서 한참 끙끙거렸어요.
examples.en: I struggled for a long time over a hard math problem.
Father seems to have a bad back and gets up groaning.

explain: 아프거나 힘들어서 낮게 앓는 소리를 낼 때 써요. 문제 때문에 힘들게 애쓰는 모습에도 써요. '끙끙대다'도 같은 뜻으로 말해요.

phrases.en: I slept groaning with a cold last night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끙끙거리다'와 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the same meaning as '끙끙거리다'.

phrases.example: 그는 몸살로 하루 종일 끙끙 앓았어요.
phrases.en: He groaned in pain all day with body aches.
phrases.nuance_ko: '앓다'와 함께 쓰면 아파서 힘들어하는 모습이 잘 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '앓다', it clearly shows someone suffering from illness.

phrases.en: I moved the refrigerator, groaning with effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무거운 것을 힘들게 옮길 때 나는 소리와 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The sound and look of struggling to move something heavy.

explain_en: It means making low moaning sounds from pain or effort. It is also used for struggling hard with a problem. '끙끙대다' means the same.

en: nape; the back of the neck

examples.en: A cold wind is blowing and the back of my neck feels chilly.
The thief was caught by the police.
The police grabbed the fleeing person by the scruff of the neck.
I was sweating, so I wiped the back of my neck with a towel.

examples.ko: 누가 목덜미를 만지는 것 같아서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled because it felt like someone touched the back of my neck.

examples.ko: 거짓말을 많이 해서 언젠가 덜미를 잡힐까 불안해요.
examples.en: I've told so many lies that I'm anxious I'll get caught someday.

explain: 몸을 말할 때는 '목덜미'라고 하는 경우가 훨씬 많고, '덜미'만 쓰는 건 주로 '덜미를 잡다/잡히다'일 때예요. '덜미를 잡히다'는 나쁜 일이 들켜서 붙잡힌다는 느낌이라 뉴스나 드라마에서도 나와요.

phrases.example: 숨기던 일이 들통나서 결국 덜미를 잡혔어요.
phrases.en: The thing I was hiding came out, and I finally got caught.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이나 비밀이 드러나서 꼼짝 못 하게 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a bad deed or secret is exposed and you are cornered.

explain_en: For the body part, people usually say '목덜미', and '덜미' alone appears mostly in '덜미를 잡다/잡히다'. '덜미를 잡히다' has the feeling of being caught for something bad, and it shows up in news and dramas too.

examples.ko: 나는 어제 뜬눈으로 밤을 새우다시피 했어요.
examples.en: I practically stayed up all night yesterday without sleeping.

examples.ko: 아기가 아파서 엄마는 뜬눈으로 아침을 맞았어요.
examples.en: The baby was sick, so Mom greeted the morning without sleeping.
Worried about the exam, I spent the whole night awake.
I stayed awake for ten hours on the plane.
Because of worry, I just lay there wide awake.
Waiting for news, I stayed awake staring at the phone.

explain: 거의 '뜬눈으로'의 꼴로 써요. 보통 '밤을 새우다', '지새우다'와 함께 나와서 걱정이나 일 때문에 한숨도 못 잤다는 느낌을 줘요. 일부러 밤을 새우는 상황보다는 잠이 안 오거나 못 자는 상황에 어울려요.

phrases.example: 합격 발표를 기다리느라 뜬눈으로 밤을 새웠어요.
phrases.en: I stayed up all night with my eyes open, waiting for the results.
phrases.nuance_ko: '눈을 뜬 채로'라는 말뜻만으로는 '한숨도 못 잤다'는 뜻이 바로 떠오르지 않아요. 걱정이나 긴장으로 잠을 못 잤을 때 쓰는 굳은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The literal words 'with eyes open' don't immediately suggest 'not sleeping at all'. It is a fixed expression for being unable to sleep due to worry or tension.

explain_en: It almost always appears as '뜬눈으로'. It usually pairs with '밤을 새우다' or '지새우다' and gives the feeling of not sleeping a wink from worry or work. It fits situations where you can't sleep more than ones where you stay up on purpose.

en: to be insensible; to be numb

examples.ko: 추운 곳에 오래 있었더니 손가락이 무감각해졌어요.
examples.en: After being in the cold for a long time, my fingers went numb.

examples.ko: 계속 나쁜 뉴스를 보니까 이제는 조금 무감각해요.
examples.en: After seeing bad news constantly, I feel a bit numb to it now.

examples.ko: 그는 다른 사람의 아픔에 무감각한 사람이 아니에요.
examples.en: He is not a person who is insensitive to other people's pain.

examples.ko: 매일 야근을 하다 보니 피곤함에도 무감각하게 됐어요.
examples.en: Working overtime every day, I became numb even to being tired.

examples.ko: 소음에 무감각해서 시끄러운 카페에서도 공부를 잘해요.
examples.en: I'm not bothered by noise, so I study well even in a loud cafe.

examples.ko: 칭찬에도 비난에도 무감각하고 싶을 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I want to be unaffected by both praise and criticism.

explain: 몸의 감각이 없을 때도, 마음이 둔해져서 아무것도 느끼지 못할 때도 써요. 몸은 '저리다', '감각이 없다'로, 마음은 '둔하다', '무뎌지다'로도 말해요. '~에 무감각하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: After sitting for a long time, my legs went numb.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무감각하다' 상태로 변해 가는 것을 말하며, 몸이 저릴 때도 마음이 둔해질 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes becoming numb, whether in the body or in feeling.

phrases.en: These days people are insensitive to small noises.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~에 무감각하다' 모양으로 어떤 일에 익숙해져서 잘 느끼지 못한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '~에 무감각하다' pattern means being so used to something that you no longer notice it.

phrases.en: My feet are so cold that I can't feel them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 몸이 무감각할 때 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler everyday way to say a body part is numb.

explain_en: It is used both when the body has lost feeling and when the mind has become dull and feels nothing. In speech, people also say '저리다' or '감각이 없다' for the body, and '둔하다' or '무뎌지다' for the mind. It takes the particle '에', as in '~에 무감각하다'.

examples.ko: 할머니가 병석에 누우신 지 한 달이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been a month since my grandmother took to her sickbed.
I heard the news that my father got up from his sickbed.
I stayed at my mother's bedside and nursed her.
When you're bedridden for long, you also lose your appetite.
After a long time in bed, he was finally discharged from the hospital.
The teacher kept reading even from his sickbed.

explain: '병석에 눕다', '병석에서 일어나다'처럼 아파서 누워 지내는 자리를 말해요. 조금 점잖은 말투라 어른의 일을 말할 때 잘 어울리고, 일상에서는 '아파서 누워 있다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My father suddenly took to his sickbed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아파서 자리에 눕게 되었다는 뜻이고, 어른께 쓰는 점잖은 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means falling ill and having to lie down; a polite, formal tone for elders.

phrases.en: Grandmother got up from her sickbed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 아프다가 나아서 다시 움직이게 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means recovering after a long illness and being up and about again.

phrases.en: I've been lying down sick since yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '병석에 눕다'를 일상에서 쉽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The plain everyday way to say 병석에 눕다.

explain_en: It refers to the place where a sick person lies, as in '병석에 눕다' or '병석에서 일어나다'. It sounds somewhat formal and suits talking about elders; in daily speech people say '아파서 누워 있다'.

examples.en: After walking all day, my feet got blistered.
My lips are blistered, so it's uncomfortable to eat.
I worked until my hands blistered, but it was worth it.

examples.ko: 요즘 피곤해서 그런지 입술이 자주 부르터요.
examples.en: Maybe because I'm tired lately, my lips often get blisters.
Please put lip balm on your blistered lips.

examples.ko: 등산화가 안 맞아서 발바닥이 부르트고 말았어요.
examples.en: My hiking boots didn't fit, and the soles of my feet ended up blistered.

explain: 피곤하거나 오래 걷고 일해서 살갗이 부풀어 오를 때 써요. 발, 손, 입술과 자주 쓰고, '부르트어'가 아니라 '부르터요'로 줄어요. '물집이 잡히다'와 비슷하지만 입술이 부르틀 때는 '부르트다'를 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I worked a lot, so my hands got blistered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 일을 해서 손의 살갗이 부풀었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when hands blister from hard work.

phrases.en: I put medicine on my blistered lips.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부르튼'은 이미 부르터 있는 상태를 꾸며 주는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 부르튼 describes something already in a blistered state.

phrases.example: 발이 부르트지 않도록 편한 신발을 신었어요.
phrases.en: I wore comfortable shoes so my feet wouldn't blister.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부르트는 것을 막고 싶을 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form for trying to prevent blistering.

explain_en: It is used when skin swells or blisters from tiredness, long walking or hard work, most often for feet, hands and lips. The conjugation is '부르터요', not '부르트어요'. It is close to '물집이 잡히다', but for lips people often use '부르트다'.

examples.ko: 가방 밖으로 우산이 삐죽 나와 있어요.
examples.en: An umbrella is sticking out of the bag.

examples.ko: 담 너머로 아이 머리가 삐죽 보였어요.
examples.en: A child's head popped up over the wall.
I stepped carefully on the rocks jutting up everywhere.
A nail is sticking out, so be careful.
The child poked his face out through the gap in the door.
My toes are poking out of my sock.

explain: 무언가가 끝이 뾰족하게 밖으로 조금 나온 모습이에요. 여러 개가 여기저기 솟아 있으면 '삐죽삐죽'이라고 해요. 입을 내미는 동작은 '삐죽거리다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: My hair is sticking up in spikes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 개가 여기저기 튀어나온 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes many things sticking out here and there.

phrases.en: I playfully stuck out my tongue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝이 조금 밖으로 나오게 내미는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The action of pushing something out just a little.

phrases.en: The shirt is sticking out of the pants.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건 끝이 밖으로 조금 나온 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the tip of something poking out.

explain_en: It describes something with a pointed tip sticking out a little. When many things stick up here and there, you say '삐죽삐죽'. Pushing out the lips is expressed with '삐죽거리다'.

examples.en: The child seems sleepy and slowly closes their eyes.
The door slid open softly.
The knot came undone by itself.
The snow melts away gently in the warm weather.

examples.ko: 그 말을 들으니 화가 스르르 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Hearing that, my anger just melted away.
I drifted off to sleep as soon as I sat on the sofa.

explain: 힘을 들이지 않고 부드럽게, 저절로 움직이거나 변하는 모습이에요. '스르르 잠들다', '스르르 녹다', '스르르 풀리다'처럼 자주 어울려요. '스르륵'은 같은 모양에 미끄러지는 소리가 조금 더 느껴지는 말이에요.

phrases.en: The baby drifted off to sleep as I held her.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들이지 않고 부드럽게 잠드는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes falling asleep gently and effortlessly.

phrases.en: The ice cream melted away softly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단단한 것이 부드럽게 저절로 녹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something hard melts softly by itself.

phrases.example: 따뜻한 차를 마시니 긴장이 스르르 풀렸어요.
phrases.en: Drinking warm tea, my tension melted away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 긴장이나 피로가 조금씩 저절로 사라질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when tension or tiredness fades away by itself.

explain_en: It describes something moving or changing smoothly by itself, without effort. It pairs often with '스르르 잠들다', '스르르 녹다' and '스르르 풀리다'. '스르륵' is the same image with a little more of the sound of sliding.

en: to faint; to black out; to swoon

examples.ko: 더운 날 오래 서 있던 학생이 갑자기 실신했어요.
examples.en: A student who had stood a long time on a hot day suddenly fainted.

examples.ko: 충격적인 소식을 듣고 어머니가 그 자리에서 실신하셨어요.
examples.en: Hearing the shocking news, my mother fainted on the spot.

examples.ko: 피를 보면 실신할 것 같아서 병원이 무서워요.
examples.en: I'm afraid of hospitals because I feel I'd faint at the sight of blood.

examples.ko: 마라톤 선수가 결승선 앞에서 실신해서 구급차를 불렀어요.
examples.en: A marathon runner collapsed before the finish line, so they called an ambulance.
I heard he couldn't eat anything until just before he blacked out.

examples.ko: 갑자기 실신한 사람을 보면 먼저 119에 전화하세요.
examples.en: If you see someone suddenly pass out, call 119 first.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '기절하다', '쓰러지다', '정신을 잃다'를 더 많이 써요. '실신하다'는 뉴스, 의료, 사고 상황처럼 격식 있게 말할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I was so surprised I almost fainted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '실신하다' 대신 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common word in daily conversation in place of 실신하다.

phrases.en: A person collapsed on the street in the hot weather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 힘이 빠져 넘어지는 모습을 말하고, 꼭 의식을 잃지 않아도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes falling down from loss of strength, not necessarily losing consciousness.

phrases.en: I hit my head when I fell and lost consciousness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의식이 없어진다는 뜻을 풀어서 쉽게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain way of saying that consciousness was lost.

explain_en: In everyday conversation people more often say '기절하다', '쓰러지다' or '정신을 잃다'. '실신하다' shows up in more formal settings such as news, medical talk and accident reports.

examples.en: The baby runs around the yard with nothing on.

examples.ko: 털을 다 깎인 양이 알몸뚱이가 돼서 추워 보였어요.
examples.en: The sheep, with all its wool sheared off, looked cold and bare.

examples.ko: 빚 때문에 모든 걸 잃고 알몸뚱이로 시작했어요.
examples.en: I lost everything because of debt and started again with nothing.

examples.ko: 겨울 나무는 잎이 다 떨어져 알몸뚱이 같아요.
examples.en: Winter trees look bare with all their leaves fallen.
You'll catch a cold if you go out with nothing on!

examples.ko: 그림 속 아이는 알몸뚱이인데도 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The child in the picture is smiling even though he has nothing on.

explain: '알몸'을 입말로 조금 세게, 또는 정답게 말하는 표현이에요. 보통은 '알몸'이 기본이고, '알몸뚱이'는 옛이야기나 만화, 말투에 감정이 들어갈 때 잘 보여요. 옷뿐 아니라 가진 게 아무것도 없는 상태를 비유할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The baby takes a bath naked.
phrases.nuance_ko: '알몸뚱이'보다 기본적이고 중립적인 말이라 어디에나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic, neutral word, usable in any situation unlike 알몸뚱이.

phrases.en: My business failed and I lost everything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이 없는 몸뿐 아니라 가진 것이 하나도 없는 상태를 비유해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Besides a body without clothes, it can mean having nothing at all.

phrases.en: The children played naked in the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 다 벗은 상태를 동사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb for being completely without clothes.

explain_en: It is a more colloquial, stronger or sometimes affectionate way to say '알몸' (naked body). '알몸' is the standard word, while '알몸뚱이' shows up in old tales, comics and emotional speech. It can also figuratively mean having nothing at all, not just no clothes.

examples.en: I waited for the bus shivering from the cold.

examples.ko: 무서운 영화를 보다가 손이 와들와들 떨렸어요.
examples.en: My hands trembled while I was watching a scary movie.

examples.ko: 발표 직전에 다리가 와들와들 떨려서 서 있기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: Right before the presentation my legs were shaking so much it was hard to stand.

examples.ko: 와들와들 떨지 말고 이 담요를 덮어요.
examples.en: Stop shivering and cover yourself with this blanket.

examples.ko: 개가 천둥소리에 놀라서 와들와들 떨고 있어요.
examples.en: The dog is startled by the thunder and trembling.

examples.ko: 차가운 물에 들어갔더니 온몸이 와들와들 떨려요.
examples.en: I went into the cold water and my whole body is shivering.

explain: 추위, 두려움, 긴장 때문에 몸이 떨리는 모양이에요. '덜덜'도 비슷하고, '벌벌'은 주로 겁이 나서 떠는 느낌이 강해요. 모두 '떨다'와 같이 써요.

phrases.example: 개가 비를 맞고 와들와들 떨고 있어요.
phrases.en: The dog got rained on and is shivering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 '떨다'를 함께 쓴 가장 흔한 짝말로, 추위나 두려움으로 몸이 떨릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 떨다, for a body trembling from cold or fear.

phrases.en: It's so cold that my hands are shaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻의 말로, 추위나 긴장으로 몸이 심하게 떨리는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word for a body shaking hard from cold or tension.

phrases.example: 무서운 개 앞에서 아이가 벌벌 떨었어요.
phrases.en: The child trembled in front of the scary dog.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겁이 나서 떠는 느낌이 더 강해서, 추위보다는 두려움에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger sense of trembling from fear, fitting fear better than cold.

explain_en: It describes the body shaking from cold, fear, or nervousness. '덜덜' is similar, and '벌벌' leans more toward trembling from fear. All of them go with '떨다'.

en: the physical body (as opposed to the mind or soul)

examples.ko: 영혼은 떠나고 육신만 남았다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a saying that the soul left and only the physical body remained.
The body has grown very weak from a long illness.

examples.ko: 육신의 피로보다 마음의 걱정이 더 컸어요.
examples.en: Worry in my heart was greater than physical tiredness.

examples.ko: 할머니는 육신은 늙어도 마음은 젊다고 하세요.
examples.en: Grandmother says that even if the body gets old, the mind stays young.
Monks and nuns practice training to discipline the body.

examples.ko: 죽은 육신 앞에서 가족들이 오래 울었어요.
examples.en: The family cried for a long time in front of the lifeless body.

explain: 육신은 영혼이나 마음과 대비해서 몸을 말할 때 써요. 그냥 몸이 아프다고 할 때는 '몸'을 쓰고, 육신은 글, 종교, 문학에서 많이 나와요. '신체'는 건강검진이나 법처럼 사실적인 상황에서 써요.

phrases.example: 일이 너무 힘들어서 육신과 영혼이 모두 지쳤어요.
phrases.en: The work was so hard that both my body and soul are exhausted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸과 마음을 대비해서 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing when contrasting body and soul.

phrases.en: He walked while enduring the pain of his body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음의 괴로움과 대비해서 몸의 아픔을 말할 때 써요. 글에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for physical suffering in contrast to mental anguish; common in writing.

phrases.en: My body is worn out after working for several days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 힘들다는 뜻이지만 '몸이 피곤하다'보다 문학적이고 무거운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the body is tired, but it sounds more literary and heavier than '몸이 피곤하다'.

explain_en: 육신 is used when contrasting the body with the soul or mind. For ordinary 'my body hurts', people say 몸; 육신 appears in writing, religion, and literature. 신체 fits factual contexts such as health checkups or law.

dis.h: literary; flesh body, contrasted with soul

p.n: The swap is everyday and neutral; the original sounds literary and stresses flesh versus spirit.

examples.ko: 그녀는 초조한 듯 손톱을 잘근잘근 씹었어요.
examples.en: She nervously chewed on her fingernails.

examples.ko: 강아지가 제 슬리퍼를 잘근잘근 물고 놀아요.
examples.en: My puppy plays by gnawing on my slippers.

examples.ko: 고기를 잘근잘근 씹어 먹으니 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: The meat tastes better when I chew it slowly.

examples.ko: 아이가 연필 끝을 잘근잘근 깨무는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: The child has a habit of nibbling the end of a pencil.
He walked along chewing gum.
She bit her lip over and over, lost in thought.

explain: 질기거나 단단한 것을 조금씩 자꾸 씹는 모양을 나타내고, 주로 '잘근잘근 씹다/깨물다'로 써요. 껌이나 질긴 고기를 씹을 때는 '질겅질겅'도 써요.

phrases.en: The baby keeps chewing on the toy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 힘으로 자꾸 깨무는 모양이에요. 아기나 강아지에게 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle, repeated biting motion, often for babies or puppies.

phrases.en: I was nervous and kept biting my lip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불안하거나 생각이 많을 때 입술을 자꾸 무는 행동을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes repeatedly biting one's lip when anxious or deep in thought.

phrases.en: I chewed the squid slowly and thoroughly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질긴 음식을 오래 씹으며 먹는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes chewing tough food for a long time while eating it.

explain_en: It shows chewing something tough or firm bit by bit, repeatedly, and mostly appears as '잘근잘근 씹다/깨물다'. For gum or chewy meat, '질겅질겅' is also used.

en: to sway; to waver; to wobble

examples.en: The bus suddenly stopped, and my body lurched.
I was so tired that I almost stumbled on the stairs.

examples.ko: 강한 바람에 나무가 휘청하는 게 보였어요.
examples.en: I saw the tree sway in the strong wind.

examples.ko: 월급은 그대로인데 교육비가 올라서 가계가 휘청해요.
examples.en: Wages stay the same while education costs rise, so household budgets are shaky.

examples.ko: 환율이 오르자 작은 회사들이 휘청하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: When the exchange rate rose, small companies began to shake.

examples.ko: 그는 휘청하더니 벽을 잡고 겨우 섰어요.
examples.en: He staggered, then grabbed the wall and barely stayed upright.

explain: 몸이 한 번 기우뚱할 때는 '휘청하다', 계속 흔들릴 때는 '휘청거리다'가 자연스러워요. 몸뿐 아니라 가계, 회사, 경제처럼 크게 흔들려서 무너질 것 같을 때도 비유로 써요. 지치거나 어지러워서 다리에 힘이 풀릴 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: A drunk person is walking along unsteadily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번이 아니라 계속 흔들릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the swaying keeps going rather than happening once.

phrases.en: I was so startled that my legs gave way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 흔들릴 만큼 힘이 빠졌을 때 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple way to say your strength drained so you wobbled.

phrases.en: When prices went up, household finances wobbled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 아니라 경제 상황이 크게 흔들릴 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for finances being badly shaken.

explain_en: For a single lurch of the body '휘청하다' is natural, while '휘청거리다' fits continuous wobbling. It is also used figuratively for households, companies or economies shaking as if they might collapse. It often appears when someone is tired or dizzy and their legs give way.
